<details class="nhsuk-details">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">Text description of this diagram</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

| Step | Where you are | What you do | What you produce |
|---|--------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | Check the playbook applies | Check it applies, then start at Phase 1. | Nothing recorded yet. |
| 2 | Phase 1 Engagement and scoping | Agree the decision, the question, what is out of scope, the deadline. | The scope and specification, with the question in one sentence. |
| 3 | Deciding your assurance level | Score the impact with your commissioner at scoping. Score the likelihood at design, or at scoping if the work is Business Critical. | The Analytical Assurance Decision Tool, with the Business Critical answer either way. |
| 4 | The checks, by level | Read the block for your level and the blocks inside it. | The quality assurance checklist, and your reviewer's time in the schedule. |
| 5 | R9 Uncertainty | Find the principal sources of uncertainty while design can still change. | Assumptions listed with their rationale and the impact if wrong. |
| 6 | Phase 3 Analysis | Your own verification and validation first, then the critical friend. | The quality assurance log, and what you did about each finding. |
| 7 | Phase 4 Delivery, communication and sign-off | State the caveats in the output itself, not only in an annex. | The output and the quality assurance statement, published from Level 3. |
| 8 | R10 Data ethics and personal data | Check the Data and AI Ethics Framework, personal data and transparency scope. | The ethics position recorded, and a transparency record drafted where in scope. |
| 9 | Phase 5 Review | Ask whether it worked, and whether it is still right. | The review record, the lessons, and any decommissioning decision. |

: The analyst's journey, step by step

Step 3 is outlined, with a note: **Business Critical.** Any one impact dimension at 4? If so, go to Business Critical analysis.

A second note, **after the last step:** What you record at the end is what the next piece of work starts from.

</div>
</details>
